metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Remains Low-End RB1 Against Titans
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was limited at practice Friday and has no injury designation heading into Week 10 against the Tennessee Titans. The young back is coming off a quieter outing, which had less to do with how he performed and more with how the game turned out. With Tuten on the injury report last week and the score being 17-3 at the half, Tuten finished with just a 36 percent snap share. He still managed a touchdown on the first drive, which salvaged his fantasy day of just 29 total yards. Unfortunately, the 1-7 Titans could present a similar game situation. However, given the potential game script being in favor of the rushing attack, it is difficult to assume Tuten won't benefit enough to produce a good fantasy outing. The Titans rank below average against the run in fantasy at 18th. Patterns suggest a slightly lower floor, but Tuten is too talented, and the situation is too beneficial for fantasy managers not to start him in Week 10.

metadata.analysis: Tuten played through the injury last week without practicing, and he'll now suit up for Week 10 after just one limited practice Friday. Chris Rodriguez (hand) also is cleared to play and could help ease the burden if Jacksonville is wary of overworking Tuten while he's banged up.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Off the Injury Report, Will Play on Sunday
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) was limited in practice on Friday but was removed from the Week 10 injury report and will play in Sunday's divisional contest against the Tennessee Titans. Tuten did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, and he also missed all three practices on a short week before suiting up and playing in last Thursday's blowout win over the Baltimore Ravens. However, he played in a season-low 36% of the offensive snaps and had a season-low 12 rushing attempts for 29 yards and a touchdown while not being targeted in the passing game for the first time all year. Fantasy managers will be hoping that Tuten is more involved this weekend against the Titans, and they should be comforted by the fact that the 23-year-old at least participated in one practice this week. The second-year RB has been a strong weekly option in fantasy football in 2026, carrying the football 122 times for 521 yards (4.3 yards per attempt) and four rushing touchdowns, adding 15 catches on 16 targets for 181 yards and another three touchdowns as a receiver. Tuten could cede valuable touches to backfield mate Chris Rodriguez Jr. again in Week 10, but fantasy managers should have him on the RB1/2 borderline now that he is officially active for Sunday's game in Nashville.

The 23-year-old's status is once again up in the air for the Jaguars' Week 10 divisional clash against the Tennessee Titans, although things could be cleared up in the next two days. metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Eyes More in Week 10 After Extra Time Off

Tuten still had a rushing touchdown and 29 yards across 12 carries. He's been a pretty solid fantasy option this season, with 521 rushing yards and four touchdowns over 122 carries, plus has caught 15 of his 16 targets for 181 yards and three more scores. Fantasy owners should expect more good showings out of Tuten, starting in Week 10 in a slightly above-average matchup against Tennessee.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Scores TD in Week 9 win
metadata.description: Tuten (ankle/foot) rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
metadata.analysis: Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Finds End Zone While Battling Injuries
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten rushed for 29 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in his team's 33-10 win against the hosting Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football. Tuten came into this one nursing a foot and ankle injury that caused him to log three straight DNPs in preparation for Week 9's clash, so it's no surprise to see him post his worst output of the campaign despite scoring his seventh all-purpose touchdown. The Virginia Tech product saw his last touch of the contest with 3:02 remaining in the third quarter, as backfield mates Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Ameer Abdullah salted away the clock over the final frame. It may not be the results fantasy managers were expecting - particularly on a rainy night. Still, as long as he escaped Thursday's outing without a setback, he should be all systems go after a mini-bye. It'd be good news too, as Jacksonville will line up against a more vulnerable Tennessee Titans rush defense for their next contest.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Will Play Thursday, Plans to "Let it Rip"
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) is good to go and will be active on Thursday night against the Baltimore Ravens after going through a pre-game workout, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Tuten went through an extensive pre-game workout and plans to "let it rip," according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The 23-year-old had a career-best day in the Week 8 blowout win over the division-rival Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, recording 104 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries while adding 55 receiving yards and another score on two receptions, but he came out of that contest with an ankle injury that made him a game-time decision for Thursday's Week 9 tilt in Baltimore. Now that Tuten is officially cleared to play against the Ravens, fantasy managers should be looking to get him into their starting lineups for the week. Going into this week's action, Tuten is the RB15 in half-PPR scoring in what has been a breakout year for him as Jacksonville's clear RB1. Managers who were ready to use Chris Rodriguez Jr. as a plug-and-play option in case Tuten was inactive can stand down now.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten gashes Colts in Week 8 rout
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten went for 104 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, adding in two receptions for 55 yards and another score in Sunday's 42-7 blowout of the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Tuten turned in the first 100-yard rushing performance of his career on Sunday while also setting a new personal best in receiving yards. The second-year speedster has now scored twice in both of the Jaguars' last two games and is up to six total touchdowns - three rushing, three receiving - for the campaign. Tuten is quickly inserting himself among the league's most potent dual-threat weapons at his position, as he's averaging nearly 18 touches and over 96 yards of offense per game.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Career-best performance in win
metadata.description: Tuten rushed 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 55 yards and another score in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Tuten looked refreshed coming out of the Week 7 bye, breaking out for a new single-game career-high rushing total. Tuten also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a rumbling 39-yard run during the second quarter where he broke several tackles, and he added his third receiving score over the last two games with a 25-yard grab as time expired in the third quarter. Tuten is up to 4.5 yards per carry after averaging a season-best 6.5 yards per tote Sunday, and he's added six total touchdowns heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Continues Breakout Season with Dominant Week 8 Showing
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten dominated in his team's 42-7 Week 8 win over the Indianapolis Colts, recording 16 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown, and hauling in two catches for 55 yards and an additional score. Tuten has been very consistent in 2026, recording at least 87 yards from scrimmage in five out of six games heading into Week 8. The star production is starting to follow now as well, as he's logged two touchdowns in consecutive games. Between Tuten's ability to make explosive plays as both a rusher and a receiver and Jacksonville's potent offensive attack, the 23-year-old profiles as a must-start running back heading into the Jaguars' Week 9 showdown against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten in Line for Second Straight Big Performance in Week 8
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten is coming off his best fantasy performance of the season as he heads into a Week 8 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts. He has been a model of consistency so far, putting up 65-plus rushing yards in his first five games. He had his worst rushing output of the season in Week 6 and the fewest carries, totaling just 39 rushing yards on 12 carries, but countered that with his best receiving game of the season. Overall, Tuten finished with 87 scrimmage yards, 16 total touches, and two receiving touchdowns. Coming off a Week 7 bye and heading into a matchup with the 22nd-ranked defense against running backs in fantasy means fantasy managers have no reason to believe that consistency will falter. The Colts are also starting to trade some of their top players while sitting at 2-5 and surrendering the Tennessee Titans their first win of the season two weeks ago. In a potential Week 8 blowout, Tuten has a chance to top his Week 6 fantasy breakout performance.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Has Topped 85 Scrimmage Yards Four Games Running
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has surpassed 85 scrimmage yards in four consecutive games as the team's lead back, accumulating 388 rushing yards, 126 receiving yards and four touchdowns through six appearances. Coming off Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, the second-year back remains a strong RB2 option in 12-team leagues against the Indianapolis Colts, with his growing receiving involvement adding to his fantasy appeal. He caught all four targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns against the Houston Texans in Week 6 after averaging just two targets per game through the first five weeks, an increased involvement in the passing game that is particularly encouraging for PPR managers. His playing time has also increased from approximately 49% of the offensive snaps over the first three games to at least 58% in each of the past three, though Chris Rodriguez Jr. remains involved, handling 11 carries for 55 yards against Houston while Tuten managed 39 yards on 12 attempts.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten hits pay dirt twice in Week 6 loss

metadata.analysis: Tuten did have a rushing touchdown called back on a holding call, limiting his rushing output. His two touchdowns receptions marked his first receiving touchdowns of the season, and is a good sign for him being more involved in the passing game in the future. metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Two receiving TDs in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
metadata.analysis: While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Adds Two Receiving Touchdowns in Week 6 Loss
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten had 12 carries for 39 yards and added four catches for 48 yards and two receiving touchdowns in his team's loss to the Houston Texans in London. Despite being held to under 50 rushing yards for the first time this season, the 2025 fourth-round draft pick is building his reputation as a multi-faceted fantasy asset. Tuten hasn't broken out just yet, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on him after battling through a tough matchup against Houston. RotoBaller listed Tuten at RB19 in the positional rankings.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Taking on a Substantially Larger Workload
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has ascended into an enormous role in the backfield, averaging 20 touches per game over the last three weeks. He has at least 9.8 points in PPR leagues in every game this year, and he ranks as the overall RB17 so far. While Tuten's ceiling hasn't been very impressive, he has maintained a high floor while operating as a consistent RB2 option in fantasy football. Most importantly, his ascension has led to a massive decrease in volume for Chris Rodriguez Jr. Once viewed as a candidate to split touches with Tuten, Rodriguez saw his snap share drop to 13% last week as he handled just two rushing attempts. As long as Tuten is healthy, he is going to continue to operate as the near-every-down back in Jacksonville while maintaining his fantasy relevance. He can be started in most leagues, regardless of matchup.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten approaches 100 yards of total offense Sunday
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten rushed for 72 yards on 22 carries, adding two receptions for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Tuten continues to prove he can shoulder the load out of the Jaguars' backfield. The second-year pro only averaged 3.3 yards on his career-high 22 carries Sunday, but he seemed to run stronger as the game progressed. For the season, Tuten is averaging 70 yards on more than 16 carries per game with a couple of touchdowns. He's a solid RB2 with upside in most fantasy formats.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Tops 90 scrimmage yards against Philly
metadata.description: Tuten carried the ball 22 times for 72 yards and caught two of three targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: The second-year back set new season highs in touches and scrimmage yards as he reached 90 in the latter category for a third straight game. Tuten has yet to have a truly huge performance this season, but he's been very steady so far as the Jaguars' No. 1 RB, collecting 349 rushing yards and two TDs on 4.3 yards per carry while adding a 9-78-0 line on 10 targets through five games. Tuten hasn't gotten into the end zone in two straight games, a streak he'll look to snap in Week 6 against the Texans.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Could Be on the Verge of a Breakout Season
metadata.description: Across four games so far in 2026, Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has recorded 60 carries for 277 yards and two touchdowns. Tuten has split rushing work to some degree with fellow Jaguars back Chris Rodriguez Jr., who has tallied 108 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season. However, Tuten has emerged as the clear lead back in Jacksonville in recent weeks, recording back-to-back games with at least 17 touches and 90 yards from scrimmage in Weeks 3 and 4. The 23-year-old currently ranks as the RB15 in half-PPR scoring and could only be on his way up as the season progresses. As long as Jacksonville's key offensive pieces around him stay healthy, Tuten profiles as a high-end RB2 with RB1 upside for fantasy managers going forward.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 91 yards in win Sunday
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 17 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
metadata.analysis: Tuten had a good game on Sunday, finishing as the team's top rusher and dominating the touches in the backfield en route to a win over the Bengals. Chris Rodriguez Jr. was the one to get into the end zone for the Jaguars, however, which was annoying for fantasy managers to see. The young running back should continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset moving forward.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Good production with 19 touches
metadata.description: Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Tuten filled his usual role as the clear lead option in Jacksonville's ground attack with aplomb, grinding out tough yards on many of his carries and also contributing a 20-yard run. He also recorded multiple receptions for the third consecutive game, and although he saw backfield mate Chris Rodriguez score the Jaguars' only rushing touchdown of the day, that came on a breakaway run from 25 yards out as opposed to in close. Tuten has at least 15 carries in three of his first four games heading into a Week 5 showdown against the Eagles in London next Sunday.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Brings Strong RB2 Appeal Into Week 4
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has been one of the steadiest parts of the offense through three weeks. He has rushed for at least 65 yards in every game, including 73 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries against New England last Sunday. Tuten also caught both of his targets for 17 yards, giving him 17 touches in the win. He leads Jacksonville with 204 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 43 attempts, and Liam Coen said Friday that the Jaguars need to keep finding ways to get him more opportunities. Cincinnati has been much better against the run this season, although Jaylen Warren did break through for 127 rushing yards against the Bengals last week. Tuten is healthy entering Sunday and sits at RB16 in RotoBaller's latest Week 4 rankings. The matchup is not a freebie, but his starting role and steady workload make him a strong RB2 option.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Firmly Establishing Himself as Jaguars' Lead Back
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten keeps giving the team reasons to leave him at the front of the backfield. He handled 15 carries for 73 yards and a touchdown against New England on Sunday, adding two catches for another 17 yards. More importantly, he played 30 offensive snaps compared with 13 for Chris Rodriguez Jr. and finished with 17 touches to Rodriguez's nine. That was not a one-week development, either. Tuten has now led Rodriguez in both snaps and touches in all three games, while averaging 4.7 yards on his 43 carries. He has rushed for 204 yards and two touchdowns so far and has not fallen below 13 carries in a game. Rodriguez will continue to get work, and Jacksonville has other backs involved on passing downs, so Tuten is not suddenly a 20-touch workhorse. Still, the lead role looks more secure now than it did entering the season. His fantasy value continues to move up heading into Sunday's matchup with Cincinnati.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten leads team in rushing Sunday
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 15 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Tuten had a good game on Sunday. He led the team in rushing yards at an efficient clip of 4.9 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a great fantasy total. He should again be started in a matchup against the Bengals next week.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Efficient effort in easy win
metadata.description: Tuten rushed 15 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Serving as the clear lead back once again, Tuten proved himself worthy of the role with a crisp performance that saw him consistently generate useful gains versus a talented Patriots front seven. Tuten capped off his fantasy-friendly effort with his second rushing touchdown of the campaign, a one-yard run with just over eight minutes remaining to close out the scoring on the afternoon. Tuten is averaging an impressive 4.7 yards per carry and is averaging a solid 16 touches through three games, rendering him an appealing option in all formats heading into a Week 4 road showdown against the Bengals next Sunday.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Continues String of RB2 Performances in Week 3
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten surpassed 65 rushing yards once again in a 35-6 victory over the New England Patriots. He finished with a season-high 73 rushing yards on 15 attempts, a touchdown, and also added two receptions for 17 yards. Tuten has been a symbol of consistency so far this season, a rare commodity at the running back position. No matter how well the offense has done overall, he has managed to get his touches and fantasy points. If Tuten can continue this run of 15-plus touches and 70-90 total yards, he will continue to be a valuable RB2 for fantasy managers. He'll be looking to produce once more in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten a Reliable RB2 Against Patriots
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has been the clear top back to start the year, and that should continue in Week 3 against the New England Patriots. The Jaguars had a rough overall offensive output against the Denver Broncos in Week 2, but that was not because of Tuten. The former combine standout finished Week 2 with 65 rushing yards and a touchdown. The only thing limiting Tuten's fantasy upside has been his lack of involvement in the passing game (just three receptions through two games). After an offensive struggle, the Jaguars could look to change their approach a bit and throw more short passes to overcome another top defense. That could mean more involvement in the passing game for Tuten. However, until he shows that, he will remain a solid RB2. Given his rushing volume in a high-powered offense, fantasy managers should feel confident starting Tuten in Week 3.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten finds the end zone in Week 2
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten carried the ball 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for minus-three yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Tuten punched in a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to give the Jaguars an early 7-0 lead. The second-year back also vastly outproduced Chris Rodriguez Jr., who had just 13 yards on six carries. Tuten has now racked up 131 rushing yards through two games. He will be a solid RB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Gets into the End Zone
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten continued to find success on the ground this weekend. Tuten rushed for 66 yards in the season opener and did more of the same on Sunday. The 23-year-old rushed 13 times for 65 yards and scored a touchdown in the loss to the Denver Broncos. Coming out of training camp, the expectation was that Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. would split up the lead back job in the backfield. That's not the case after two games; Rodriguez has only registered 36 yards on 12 carries. Tuten has piled up 131 yards and should continue to pull away with the lead back job in Jacksonville. Fantasy managers should be able to plug him in as a solid RB2 for the Week 3 matchup against the New England Patriots.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Records rush TD in loss
metadata.description: Tuten rushed 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for minus-3 yards in the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Tuten worked as the Jaguars' clear lead back for the second time in as many games to open the season, even though his rushing workload was relatively modest Sunday. Tuten got into the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard run early in the second quarter, and he was efficient overall against a high-caliber defense. Tuten figures to remain in the same role for a Week 3 home showdown against the defending AFC champion Patriots next Sunday.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten a Steady Fantasy Option with Large Workload
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten played less than 50% of the snaps in Week 1, but he handled 15 carries in the season-opening win and cemented himself as the team's primary ball-carrier. Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. handled similar snap shares, but the latter had just six touches. At this point, there's no question that Tuten is the one and only Jaguars running back worth starting in fantasy football. The only concern is that the Jaguars throw the ball so much, so Tuten may not have a ton of touchdown opportunities on the ground. Nevertheless, he's a high-end RB3/flex based on rushing alone, and the touchdown upside could vault him to the low-end RB2 range. As it stands, he ranks as the RB25 in RotoBaller's latest fantasy football rankings for his Week 2 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Looking to Build on Busy Week 1 Against Broncos
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten will face what was previously considered a tough Broncos defense, until the Kansas City Chiefs offense absolutely dominated them in Week 1. The rushing attack was the main reason for their success, so maybe the Jaguars will try to follow the same blueprint. However, Tuten is talented, but not on the same level as Kenneth Walker, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. still has a role in the offense. The second-year back didn't play in last year's matchup between these two teams, but the passing attack was the main reason for the Jaguars winning 34-20. Tuten only had one reception last week against the Browns, but it's hard to put too much stock in that given that quarterback Trevor Lawrence only had 23 passing attempts. If Tuten can be involved in both the rushing and passing attack in Week 2, he should produce a solid RB2 fantasy performance.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Looks Like Jaguars' Lead Back
metadata.description: After the Jacksonville Jaguars' 34-10 blowout win over the visiting Cleveland Browns on Sunday in the Week 1 season opener, John Shipley of Sports Illustrated wrote that "for now, it looks like" running back Bhayshul Tuten is the team's lead back. Tuten outsnapped Chris Rodriguez Jr. 28 (49%) to 23 (40%) and out-touched him 16 to six. However, as third-down back LeQuint Allen Jr., who had only one snap, gets healthier, the distribution of snaps could shift more. For now, Tuten's fantasy football stock is rising, especially since head coach Liam Coen has been praising him. "I think Tuten ran his tail off. He ran hard. The first run of the day, the first play of the day, I think we maybe had a chance to keep that thing inside, but there was a little color that he did see that allowed him to bounce it. I don't think he missed many reads, personally," Coen said. The 23-year-old handled 15 carries for 16 yards and caught his lone target for 22 yards. It was not a huge game by any means, but it was efficient as the lead back. Tuten is definitely the most fantasy-relevant back in Jacksonville right now, but he faces a difficult Week 2 matchup against the Denver Broncos and their stout defense.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 66 yards on the ground in win
metadata.description: Bhayshul Tuten ran 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also caught his only target for 22 yards.
metadata.analysis: Tuten led the Jags in rushing attempts in the win, but didn't have much to show in terms of fantasy scoring in half- or full-PPR formats. But to be fair, he was efficient in his touches, and it's likely that better days are ahead for the apparent Jags RB1.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten - Impressive as lead back in win
metadata.description: Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards and brought in his only target for 22 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Any questions surrounding the potential workload split in the Jaguars' ground attack were definitively answered for the time being Sunday, as Tuten put together an impressively efficient performance and outpaced backfield mate Chris Rodriguez by nine carries despite seeing his day come to an early end due to the lopsided score. Tuten was able to consistently generate productive runs, but he'll have a much stiffer test on the road against the Broncos in a Week 2 matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten the Clear Top Back Against Browns
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten played well in his first game as the full-time starter, finishing with 15 carries for 66 yards and a 22-yard catch. The passing game and defense were the primary reasons for the Jaguars dominating the Browns, but Tuten was involved just enough to muster a respectable fantasy outing. What is most reassuring is the fact that he finished with nine more carries than Chris Rodriguez Jr., who was considered a potential roadblock to Tuten getting high volume. The rookie combine standout will look to build on this performance in Week 2 against the Denver Broncos.

metadata.title: Bhayshul Tuten Holds RB2 Upside Against Browns
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten will look to prove he is capable of being a starter against the Cleveland Browns in year two under Liam Coen. Many fantasy managers are drafting him high due to his potential volume, but it will take a week of good production and good volume for managers to truly be able to trust him going forward. Tuten was solid in limited action last year as a rookie, putting up four touchdowns and 4.9 yards per carry in the one game he had double-digit carries. He also had a fantastic combine entering the league, so there are plenty of reasons to believe in the second-year pro this season. In a game against one of the worst teams in the NFL, Tuten has a chance to show his breakout potential in what should be a run-heavy game script against the Browns. Even though he may share work with Chris Rodriguez Jr., he should see enough carries to provide RB2 value.
